title: When a Symptom Needs a Doctor
hook: Most everyday symptoms pass on their own. The skill worth having is recognizing the red flags that mean don't wait — call for help now.
key_points: Certain signs are medical emergencies: call emergency services immediately.
Red flags include chest pain, trouble breathing, sudden weakness or confusion, and severe bleeding.
Signs of a stroke — face drooping, arm weakness, speech difficulty — mean act fast.
When unsure, a nurse line or your provider can help you judge urgency.
content_html: Knowing when to ride out a symptom and when to seek help is one of the most useful pieces of health literacy. Most things resolve on their own — but a short list of warning signs should never be ignored.
extra_html: The NHS distinguishes everyday complaints from emergencies, and the emergencies are worth memorizing: severe chest pain, sudden difficulty breathing, heavy bleeding that won't stop, sudden weakness, numbness, or confusion, a loss of consciousness, or signs of a stroke. For stroke, the FAST test is the shorthand — Face drooping, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty, Time to call for help — because rapid treatment can limit lasting damage. Any of these means calling emergency services right away rather than waiting to "see how it goes." For the large middle ground — a stubborn fever, a worrying but non-emergency symptom, uncertainty about a child or older relative — the NHS points to nurse advice lines and your regular provider, who can help you gauge how urgent something really is. The principle is simple: know the red flags cold, and when in doubt, ask.

related.title: Hands-Only CPR
related.hook: If an adult collapses and isn't breathing, you don't need training certificates or rescue breaths — just two steps that can double or triple their chance of survival.

related.title: Cold, Flu, or COVID?
related.hook: They share a lot of symptoms, but colds, flu, and COVID-19 differ in how fast they hit and how hard — and telling them apart can change what you do next.

related.title: Recognizing Depression and Anxiety
related.hook: Depression and anxiety are among the most common — and most treatable — health conditions. Knowing the signs is the first step to getting help that works.

flashcards.prompt: Which symptom is a medical emergency that means calling for help immediately?

choices.text: Chest pain or sudden difficulty breathing

flashcards.explanation_html: The NHS lists chest pain, breathing difficulty, severe bleeding, sudden weakness or confusion, and signs of stroke as emergencies needing immediate help.

flashcards.prompt: What does the stroke warning 'FAST' stand for?
flashcards.back_html: Face drooping, Arm weakness, Speech difficulty, Time to call emergency services. Sudden onset of any of these means act immediately.
